title: GemSim host transport signal and event extension
scope: bounded bridge-owned signal lifecycle and wait completion events only

capability.name: SIGNAL_EVENT_V1
capability.negotiation: selected if and only if both offered and required by the client; offered-only is not selected; required-not-offered is the base subset failure; independent of QUEUE_CONTROL_V1 and SIMULATED_MEMORY_V1

transport.crc: base protocol CRC-32C over the complete frame

condition_rules.wire_domain: the exact u64 bit pattern of the signed value
condition_rules.LT: observed < compare_value using signed int64 ordering
condition_rules.GTE: observed >= compare_value using signed int64 ordering
condition_rules.arithmetic: no arithmetic or overflow is involved in condition evaluation

STORE.completion: only a previously armed WAIT may complete; STORE itself has no completion

opcode_constraints.failure_ack: known nonzero status; protocol version 1.0; echo request_id, opcode, signal_id, generation, and sequence from the structurally decoded request; value, ready, and sim_tick are zero; response header uses actual daemon UUID, current connection ID, and actual epoch; no descriptor; no completion follows

ack_rules.common: exactly one 144-byte SIGNAL_ACK with no ancillary data; framing and signal version 1.0, known status, request_id echo, actual daemon UUID, current connection ID, actual epoch, and all reserved fields are exact
ack_rules.CREATE_success: status OK; assigned slot is in 1 through 1024; generation is nonzero and new; sequence zero; value exactly echoes the initial signed bit pattern; ready zero; sim_tick is an opaque admission tick
ack_rules.DESTROY_success: status OK; identity echoes; sequence, value, and ready are zero; sim_tick is an opaque admission tick
ack_rules.LOAD_success: status OK; identity echoes; sequence and ready are zero; value is the event-queue-ordered current signed bit pattern; sim_tick is an opaque admission tick
ack_rules.STORE_success: status OK; identity echoes; sequence and ready are zero; value exactly echoes the committed signed bit pattern; sim_tick is the store admission tick and follows sim_tick_rules.store_ack
ack_rules.WAIT_success: status OK; identity and sequence echo; value is the admission snapshot; ready is exactly zero or one and equals the signed predicate result; sim_tick is admission tick T and follows sim_tick_rules.wait_ack
ack_rules.failure: status is a known nonzero base status; opcode, signal_id, generation, and sequence echo; value, ready, and sim_tick are zero
ack_rules.runtime_validation: any ACK shape, identity, request correlation, reserved-field, value, ready, descriptor, or status mismatch after send poisons and closes the session; sim_tick is validated only by sim_tick_rules and the locally known completion correlation

sim_tick_rules.opaque_lifecycle_ack: Successful CREATE, LOAD, and DESTROY ACK sim_tick is the daemon admission tick and is opaque to the runtime; it may be any u64 value, including UINT64_MAX, and the client does not compare it with a locally predicted tick.
sim_tick_rules.store_ack: A successful STORE ACK sim_tick is the daemon admission tick. If that STORE is the first store to satisfy an armed WAIT, its tick S MUST be below UINT64_MAX so S+1 is representable and the runtime records S for completion validation; if it satisfies no armed WAIT, its tick is opaque and may be any u64 value, including UINT64_MAX.
sim_tick_rules.wait_ack: A successful WAIT ACK sim_tick is admission tick T and MUST be below UINT64_MAX because the accepted wait owes a completion at T+1. The runtime enforces this bound; it does not predict T.
sim_tick_rules.immediate_completion: For a WAIT ACK with ready=1, completion sim_tick MUST equal the locally received WAIT ACK tick T plus one, and the completion value MUST equal the ACK snapshot.
sim_tick_rules.armed_completion: For a WAIT ACK with ready=0, completion sim_tick MUST equal the locally received satisfying STORE ACK tick S plus one, and MUST be strictly greater than the locally received WAIT ACK tick T. The runtime compares only these known ticks.
sim_tick_rules.failure_ack: Every failed ACK has sim_tick zero.

completion_rules.message: SIGNAL_COMPLETION exists only for a successfully acknowledged WAIT
completion_rules.identity: request_id, signal_id, generation, and sequence exactly echo the originating WAIT
completion_rules.result: status OK, opcode WAIT, ready zero, and value satisfies the stored signed predicate
completion_rules.immediate: if WAIT_ACK ready is one, completion value equals the ACK snapshot and completion sim_tick equals ACK sim_tick plus one
completion_rules.armed: if WAIT_ACK ready is zero, the first later STORE whose committed value satisfies the predicate captures that value and completion sim_tick equals that STORE admission tick plus one; completion sim_tick is strictly greater than WAIT_ACK sim_tick
completion_rules.exactly_once: once ready, a wait is never re-evaluated; later stores cannot change its captured completion value; the wait remains counted and keeps DESTROY busy after its completion is queued until that complete frame is successfully sent
completion_rules.failure_completion: forbidden; any non-OK or otherwise noncanonical SIGNAL_COMPLETION poisons the runtime session

error_precedence: DROP_AND_CLOSE invalid envelope, CRC, message type, frame or payload length, header reserved field, uncorrelatable request, MSG_TRUNC, MSG_CTRUNC, malformed ancillary structure, or any descriptor attached to a signal record
MALFORMED correlatable flags, payload reserved field, opcode, opcode-canonical-field, or WAIT condition error
PROTOCOL_STATE stale, foreign, destroyed, out-of-range signal, or non-next WAIT sequence
BUSY destroy with pending wait or conflicting wait on the same signal
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED signal slot, generation, or session pending-wait ceiling
INTERNAL completion-tick overflow or event scheduling failure

semantics.event_handle: there is no separate event handle in version 1; SIGNAL_COMPLETION is the event primitive
semantics.signal_identity: lowest-free slot IDs 1 through 1024 may be reused only with a new daemon-lifetime monotonic nonzero generation; generation never wraps
semantics.ownership: signal identity is scoped to the owning client file descriptor generation and negotiated connection
semantics.event_queue: PollEvent only schedules service; all decode, lifecycle, load, store, wait admission, predicate evaluation, ACK construction, and completion construction occur on the gem5 event queue
semantics.ordering: record service gives CREATE, DESTROY, LOAD, STORE, and WAIT a single deterministic order; STORE commits before its ACK is constructed and before newly satisfied waits are queued
semantics.wait_admission: WAIT at UINT64_MAX is INTERNAL and changes neither the per-signal sequence nor waiter state; otherwise an immediately satisfied wait captures its admission value and becomes due one tick later, while an unsatisfied wait becomes armed
semantics.store_overflow: at UINT64_MAX a STORE that would first satisfy an armed wait is INTERNAL and leaves both signal value and waiter unchanged; a STORE that satisfies no waiter may commit at UINT64_MAX
semantics.wait_resources: at most one armed, scheduled, or outbound-but-not-yet-sent wait exists per signal and at most eight exist in the session; a wait releases its resource only after the complete completion frame is sent; rejected waits do not advance the per-signal sequence
semantics.destroy: DESTROY is BUSY while a wait or its callback is pending
semantics.callback_validation: before emission, a callback validates owner file descriptor generation, signal slot and generation, wait sequence, and originating request_id
semantics.disconnect: disconnect, completion send failure, or outbound overflow cancels every wait and callback and releases all signals owned by the client file descriptor generation
semantics.request_id: the HELLO-seeded session-wide strictly increasing tracker is shared by queue, memory, and signal requests and never wraps; every structurally, version, identity, and capability-admitted request consumes its ID even when lifecycle, BUSY, resource, or tick validation rejects it
semantics.outbound_bound: eight queued-but-unsent prior queue completions, eight newly admitted queue completions, eight signal waits or completions, and one synchronous ACK fit the fixed maximum of twenty-five outbound records; queue completion construction releases its inflight command before socket send, so both queue cohorts are counted
semantics.runtime_handle_ownership: the opaque signal handle is unique ownership; copied aliases must not be passed after successful destroy or instance close

runtime_wait.serialization: callers serialize queue, memory, and signal operations on one instance
runtime_wait.deadline: one CLOCK_MONOTONIC absolute deadline is formed once after synchronous validation; expired deadline precedes simultaneous cancellation and both are checked before consuming a buffered completion
runtime_wait.before_ack: failure before a complete record send is determinate; after a complete send, timeout, cancellation, EOF, or noncanonical ACK before the canonical terminal ACK poisons and closes the session
runtime_wait.after_ack: timeout or cancellation while awaiting a successfully acknowledged WAIT completion leaves the wait and any buffered completion pending and keeps the session reusable; EOF or protocol failure poisons
runtime_wait.retry: the same signal, condition, and compare value retries the existing wait without allocating a request ID or sending another WAIT; a different predicate and DESTROY return BUSY while the wait is pending; LOAD and STORE remain allowed
runtime_wait.publication: wait result output is published only after the complete SIGNAL_COMPLETION validates; timeout, cancellation, and protocol failure expose no partial result

interleave.allowed: while awaiting any queue, memory, or signal ACK or any queue or signal completion, only a canonical completion for a previously acknowledged pending queue command or signal wait may be validated and bounded-buffered
interleave.forbidden: a completion using the active request_id before its ACK, an unknown record type, a foreign or duplicate completion, or any noncanonical completion poisons and closes the session
interleave.buffer_retry: deadline and cancellation are checked before a buffered completion is consumed; timeout or cancellation leaves it pending
